why: Choose-or-skip each candidate once with a running remainder: the Combination Sum II backtracking template, where sorting lets you prune once a value exceeds the remainder and skip equal values at the same depth to avoid duplicate combinations.
hints: Each position can be used at most once, but [1,7] built from either 1 counts only once. How do you stop the same value list from being built twice?
Sort candidates. In the DFS, loop i from start; skip nums[i] if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i-1] (same value already tried at this depth), and recurse with i + 1 because positions are single-use.

DFS(start, remain): record path when remain == 0; break when nums[i] > remain (all values positive). Sorted traversal outputs the combinations already in lexicographic order. Worst case O(2^n) for n <= 20.
pitfalls: Skip duplicates only among siblings (i > start), not along a path, or [1,1,6] disappears.
Recurse with i + 1, not i: each position is single-use.
Return [] (not [[]]) when nothing sums to target.
